messages:
jordan: FYI ACME-prod users reporting 429/503 spikes on their Dedicated pool (us-east-2). Started ~06:01 UTC, error rate climbing fast. Suspect KV cache pressure from long-context requests.

maria: oncall taking a look. Can you paste the customer's repro and any trace ids?

jordan: customer says their ingest job started sending many 16k token prompts for batch rerank. Repro steps they gave: 
1) POST /v1/generate with model=redwood-large-dedicated
2) context_length ~16k, concurrency 12
3) payloads arrive in short burst (~30s)
They attached trace: trace_id=trc_0a7f9c. Logs: ```KV_MANAGER: mem_used=93.7% evictions/s=780 alloc_fail=12 backpressure=1 queue_len=84```

samir: that backpressure flag is our runtime throttling when KV eviction can't keep up. Looks like autoscaler didn't add replicas quickly enough. I'm pulling autoscaler logs now.

infra-bot: [autoscaler] pool=dedicated-us-east-2-acme, desired=6, ready=4, pending_scale_up=2, last_scale_event=2026-03-17T05:59:10Z, cooldown=120s

maria: so autoscaler desired was 6 but only 4 ready. Pending scaleups stuck for ~2m during spike. Could be scheduling or GPU allocation lag.

ben: Customer says they also saw auth-related 5xx for a few calls but those look downstream of the same throttling. Ticket linked: CS-2247. I put them on reduced concurrency as temporary mitigation.

kyle: quick mitigation options: 1) ask customer to reduce context_length to <=8k, 2) route a % of traffic to smaller model variant (redwood-medium) to lower KV pressure, 3) temporarily bump dedicated pool min_replicas to 6 for them.

ashley: I'll coordinate with ACME PM about temporary capacity increase. They want minimal user impact. Send me the cost estimate for bumping reserved capacity by 2 GPUs for 24h.

samir: diag notes: KV memory fragmentation high w/ many long-context allocations -> frequent small evictions. We should run defrag job and consider lowering per-request KV prealloc or switching to slab allocator. Relevant logs: ```kv_frag_pct=27.4 kv_chunks=18432 kv_free_small=3200```.

maria: created incident stub in incidents channel and assigned to eng-runtime. Incident id: INC-2026-1039. Adding triage checklist: collect heap profiles, allocation traces, kernel metrics, pod events, and incr autoscaler history.

samir: quick patch we can try: reduce KV eviction threshold from 90% -> 85% for this pool to give earlier evictions and avoid alloc_fails. Will push a config change to canary host first.

infra-bot: change_request: pool=dedicated-us-east-2-acme kv_eviction_threshold=85% target_hosts=[host-23] status=queued

jordan: customer accepted routing 20% of traffic to redwood-medium and reducing concurrency from 12->6. That dropped error rate immediately. Will monitor for 30m.

ben: logged follow-ups on CS-2247: (1) migrate long-context customers to a dedicated KV-larger profile, (2) add autoscaler alert when pending_scale_up > 0 for >60s, (3) implement periodic KV defrag.

kyle: also adding a note to model-onboarding: flag models that frequently use >8k context so we can recommend different defaults.

maria: summary for postmortem: root cause = KV cache pressure from bursts of long-context requests + autoscaler scale-up lag + fragmentation exacerbating eviction inefficiency. Mitigations applied: traffic shift, reduced concurrency, temporary kv_eviction_threshold change, customer capacity bump in progress. Next steps: ENG-RUNTIME to implement defrag and allocator improvement, INFRA to add autoscaler pending alert, CS to offer capacity plan to ACME.

ashley: sending customer update now. Thanks all :thumbsup:
